newsitem.title: UK: UK bankers regret Euro body reserve comments.
newsitem.headline: UK bankers regret Euro body reserve comments.

text.p: The British Bankers Association (BBA), which represents more than 300 banks, said on Friday it was disappointed that the European Monetary Institute (EMI) "continues to entertain the idea of reserve requirements".
"The imposition of reserve requirements is unnecessary for the efficient conduct of monetary policy and threatens to distort the market," Tim Sweeney, the BBA's director general, said in a statement.
"In an open market it will also siphon business out of the Euro area," he added.

This view echoed the Bank of England which said it continued to argue against reserve requirements. "We regard unremunerated reserve requirements as particularly damaging, through the tax they impose on the business done through the institutions subject to the requirements," it said.

The BBA's Sweeney said the EMI had delivered "a comprehensive and impressive document" and there was much in the proposals which it could support, in particular the emphasis on a market-oriented approach.

The EMI said that in considering the efficiency of a potential minimum reserve system, the European Central Bank (ECB) "might need to impose reserve ratios on a broad range of liabilities and institutions".

It said it had seen a need to study further the extension of the definition in the relevant article "so as to allow the ECB to subject a broader range of financial institutions than credit institutions alone to reserve requirements".
"The terms and conditions of the...minimum reserve system, including the rate of remunerations of required reserves, if any, would be uniform throughout the euro area," it added.
The BoE said it regarded remunerated reserve requirements as "inferior to market approaches which can be used to achieve the same objectives".
